title: Silo-level fail-fast admission controller for SLO-driven multi-region failover
creator: Leila Morales
description:
Goal: Implement a silo-scoped admission controller that enforces SLO-aware, fail-fast behavior for Dedicated/Private control planes to reduce blast radius during overloads and enable deterministic multi-region failover.

Motivation:
- Current tenant-level protection is reactive and slow to converge during cross-silo overloads; upgrades and noisy neighbors can cause cascading latency and missed SLOs.
- For Dedicated/Private customers we need a predictable per-silo circuit breaker that: (1) enforces admission budgets tied to SLO/error budgets, (2) provides deterministic decisions for region-level failover, and (3) emits clear signals for observability and automated remediation.

Scope:
- Admission controller library (sidecar/agent or control-plane hook) that lives per-silo (a silo is a physical or logical grouping for a set of customer capacity units) and applies admission rules for incoming inference requests.
- SLO models supported: p95 latency, p99 latency, and request error rate. Policies map remaining error/latency budget to admission rate caps and circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Integration points: frontend load balancer (quota gating), control-plane routing (failover triggers), Console dashboard and alerting, rollout automation for upgrades.
- Out of scope: tenant billing changes, model-level adaptive quantization (handled by Optimize).

Design highlights:
1) Fast path enforcement: Controller computes an admission_score per silo from streaming metrics (rolling window 30s) and enforces a fast admission decision (<2ms added tail latency). Implementation uses a lightweight token-bucket with dynamic refill driven by error-budget burn rate.
2) Multi-tier circuit breakers: GREEN (no action), YELLOW (probabilistic shedding at configured ratio), RED (hard reject new requests; existing in-flight finish). Transitions are hysteretic to avoid flapping; cooldown backoff is exponential with jitter.
3) Region-aware failover hooks: When RED persists for >30s and retry budget is exhausted, emit a structured signal to control-plane routing for automated regional redirect to standby capacity or compatible model variant.
4) Observability: expose per-silo admission metrics (allowed, rejected, shed_rate, p95, p99, error_rate, circuit_state) to Console; wire into SLO dashboards and automatic runbooks.
5) Safety: admission controller can be run in a monitoring-only mode and flipped to enforcement via a feature-flagged rollout; default for Private customers is monitoring-only until signed off.

Telemetry and SLO mapping:
- Primary SLOs: p95 latency <= configured target_ms, error_rate <= configured_target%.
- Admission decisions derived from: current p95, request backlog, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate.
- Decision equation documented in design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.internal.redwood/silo-admit-design

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Canary in staging with monitoring-only mode. Create PRs for metrics and dashboard.
- Phase 1: Canary enforcement on non-sensitive customer silos (1% capacity) with fast rollback policy.
- Phase 2: Regional canaries + automated failover enabled for test regions.
- Phase 3: Global rollout across Dedicated tenants; Private customers opt-in via upgrade bundle.

Testing:
- Unit tests for decision logic and state-machine transitions.
- Chaos tests: simulated noisy neighbor + slow kernel scenarios to validate hysteresis and failover signals.
- Load tests: replay production-like request distributions to validate token-bucket behavior under p95 pressure.

Runbook and operator controls:
- Single-click revert in Console that switches controller to monitoring-only and drains probabilistic shedding.
- Emergency throttle override that opens admission for critical admin keys.
- Troubleshooting checklist in Confluence with runbooks and diagnostic queries.

Success criteria:
- Reduce cross-silo incident mean time to recovery by 30% in simulated overloads.
- Prevent SLO violations from propagating beyond originating silo in 95% of tests.
- No >5% increase in client-observed error rate during rollout (due to misconfigured shed ratios).
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller computes decisions and enforces token-bucket within 2ms added latency in 95th percentile
Console shows per-silo admission metrics and a default dashboard with alerting for circuit_state changes
Automated region failover signal is emitted when RED persists >30s and verified in integration test
Feature-flagged rollout completed: monitoring-only -> 1% enforcement canary -> toggled enforcement across canaries
Chaos/load tests demonstrate SLO containment in 95% of runs with documented mitigations for regressions

2025-11-15 Ops: Opened a test incident while running chaos test; admission controller transitioned to RED and emitted failover signal as expected. Logged runbook steps: https://confluence.internal.redwood/silo-admit-runbook

2025-11-17 Design decision: Start with sidecar agent to allow Private installations without control-plane changes; long-term plan to upstream into control-plane admission path. Documented trade-offs in design doc.
